why_scored: OpenCode's own voice is a GPT-Live call that needs a paid OpenAI API key or a paid OpenCode Console account, and it only steers OpenCode sessions, so it cannot run free or type into another app. Hex (anomalyco/hex) is the OpenCode team's local dictation app; it runs free and headless on Linux, so it is scored in its place, with its default English model.

engines.silas: Silas, Parakeet TDT 0.6B v3 Q4_K_M GGUF on transcribe.cpp, CPU, through the dictation path (silas-bench run)
engines.rival: Hex 3.4.0 release binary, Parakeet Unified English 0.6B Q8_0 GGUF on transcribe.cpp, CPU (bench/engines/hex_engine.py)
engines.opencode_voice: OpenCode Desktop voice call: gpt-live-1 over WebRTC, delegating to gpt-6.1-sol (not run: paid key)

machine.name: chapel1
machine.gpu: none used (Hex fell back to its CPU engine; Silas runs on CPU)

silas_fast.how: silas-bench run --fast, 2026-11-22 main (accuracy; what CI compares)

silas_real_time.how: silas-bench run, paced in real time, 2026-11-18 on a quiet chapel1 (times, memory, CPU)

rival_api.how: bench/engines/hex_engine.py: a warm `hex service`; each clip played in real time, then after the 200 ms tail sent whole to POST /transcriptions, timed from key up. 2026-11-22, paired clip by clip with under-load/silas-real-time.jsonl.gz on a busy chapel1, so its times are not recorded (accuracy only)

rival_cli.how: bench/engines/hex_engine.py --cli: one `hex transcribe` per clip against the warm service, 2026-11-18 on a quiet chapel1 (memory, CPU, and a ceiling on Hex's quiet wait; its times come in ~612 ms poll steps, so the check reads them as unmeasured)

rival_one_shot.how: bench/engines/hex_engine.py --one-shot: no service, 2026-11-22 (accuracy only; Hex keeps its better run per metric)

time_to_first_word_ms.what: median, key down to the first text available. Silas: its first piece or its final text. Hex's file path is batch: clip length plus its wait.
time_to_first_word_ms.opencode_voice_note: not measured: needs a paid key. A GPT-Live call streams, but its words go to a voice agent, not to a text field.
time_to_first_word_ms.note: Hex is now timed poll free through its local API, but chapel1 stayed busy all day (load average about 10 from fleet CI and a model catalog run that skips the bench lock), and busy times are refused by --record. Not scored: undecided. Hex's quiet ceiling (6571.0 ms) is above Silas's 6476.3 ms, so either could lead.
time_to_first_word_ms.rival_quiet_ceiling_note: 2026-11-18, quiet: the 200 ms tail plus each clip's polled `hex transcribe` time, which can only be later than the model's answer (hex-cli.jsonl.gz)

wer.what: word error rate on ref_verbatim, pooled over the subset's speech clips (score.py's default normalization)
wer.opencode_voice_note: not measured: gpt-live-1 is a paid cloud model with no free tier in the source

punctuation_f1.what: F1 of sentence marks (comma, stop, question) on ref_formatted, words aligned (rivals.py)
punctuation_f1.opencode_voice_note: not measured: its text is rewritten by an agent before a session sees it

formatted_error.what: token error rate on ref_formatted, case and punctuation counted (score.py)

typing_ms.what: median time from the final text to the text in the focused field on X11 (Xvfb). Silas: measured, its typer at the default "fast" pace. Hex: modeled from its X11 paste code, since Hex's paste can't run without its desktop app: the 60 ms sleep between taking the clipboard and pressing Ctrl+V, then four XTest events (Ctrl and V, down and up) at the rate Silas's typer sends keys with no wait. Waits that run after the text is in, Silas's 60 ms drain and Hex's 100 ms settle, are not counted on either side.
typing_ms.opencode_voice_note: none: a call never puts text in another app; its delegate sends messages to OpenCode sessions only

rival_model.step: save the old clipboard (instant when it is empty or still holds Hex's last paste; an X11 read of up to 1 s otherwise, not counted)
wait for modifier keys no Hex shortcut holds (none held after key up)
Ctrl+V: four XTest events, each checked, about two keys at Silas's measured 803 keys a second with no wait

rival_after_text.step: settle before the next paste may replace the clipboard (runs after Ctrl+V)
put the old clipboard back, on its own thread

silas_after_text.step: let the last synthetic events drain before reading the keyboard again (runs after the last key)

typing_ms.rival_before_note: 2026-11-18 figure: one Ctrl+V timed as one key event by the typer before XTest, leaving out the 60 ms sleep before it. Kept for comparison; the scored figure is the model above.

opencode_voice_steps.step: install an OpenCode Desktop build that is not the prod channel
turn on the Voice calls experiment in the developer Knobs panel (off by default)
give the server an OpenAI API key or an OpenCode Console sign-in (both paid; a ChatGPT sign-in is refused)
